findings.summary: A full-viewport consent wall hides all news on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the consent dialog occupying the usable viewport before any article or headline can be read.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a compact, non-modal privacy notice and defer optional processing until an explicit choice.

findings.summary: Rejecting tracking leads to a pay-or-consent choice rather than a straightforward refusal.
findings.evidence: The active consent walkthrough changed “Odrzucam” into two choices: “Nie chcę płacić, jednak akceptuję zgody” or “Nadal odrzucam, chcę zapłacić”. Core content remains gated.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer an equally prominent, free “reject optional processing” path; separate essential access, subscription value, and tracking consent.

findings.summary: The narrow layout overflows by 604 px.
findings.evidence: At a 360×800 viewport the layout primitive measured scrollWidth 964 px versus clientWidth 360 px, with horizontalOverflowPx 604. The mobile screenshot is visibly clipped.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed desktop-width constraints from the consent and page shell; use intrinsic sizing, min-inline-size:0, and responsive max-inline-size:100%.

findings.summary: The first-load privacy UI ignores the requested dark color scheme.
findings.evidence: Light and prefers-color-scheme:dark screenshots are byte-identical and retain a white consent surface even though the underlying site exposes a manual dark-mode control.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply color-scheme and preference-driven surface/text tokens to the consent layer as well as the main site.

findings.summary: Navigation changes are abrupt rather than transition-guided.
findings.evidence: DOM and CSS probes found no View Transition usage, while the representative flow uses conventional full-document links between the listing and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin listing-to-article navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no visible scroll progress or scroll-state-aware chrome.
findings.evidence: The 10,834 px homepage screenshot shows a long feed, while DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative reading/feed progress affordance and adapt sticky chrome using scroll-state queries where supported.

findings.summary: Overlays use custom role-based elements rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The structured probe found a DIV role=dialog for navigation and LABEL role=button controls; Lighthouse also flagged the menu label role as inappropriate.
findings.suggestedFix: Use button plus popover for the navigation drawer and dialog for truly modal consent, preserving native focus and dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Repeated promotional and placeholder modules dilute the news feed.
findings.evidence: The full-page capture shows repeated WP placeholder blocks, dense recommendation modules, and a large red promotional panel interleaved with headlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve the primary feed for editorial content, collapse empty ad slots, and defer secondary recommendation modules until requested or near viewport.

findings.summary: Reusable cards rely on viewport styling only.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe counted zero container rules across a homepage that reuses news cards in hero, narrow-column, and grid contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards containment and adapt their composition with @container rather than duplicating viewport breakpoints.

findings.summary: Some touch targets are too small or too tightly spaced.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found footer links with safe clickable height about 20.8 px, below the 24 px audit floor, and reported two target-size failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target padding and spacing to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary controls.

findings.summary: The primary read-news journey is blocked by a two-step consent/payment detour.
findings.evidence: The homepage-to-article walkthrough cannot reach content until the user accepts tracking or continues into a paid rejection path.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users read core content after a direct optional-processing refusal; make subscription an independent offer.

findings.summary: Lab loading performance misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 9,193 ms, FCP 5,554 ms and performance score 0.56; the separate trace measured LCP 3,045 ms and FCP 1,927 ms, still above the 2.5 s good LCP threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP render delay, prioritize the hero image, and remove nonessential work from the critical path.

findings.summary: Main-thread work includes long tasks and forced reflow.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded two long tasks, longest 165 ms and TBT 126 ms; Lighthouse reported 212 ms TBT and 40.7 ms forced reflow in the main bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Batch DOM reads/writes, break up long tasks, and schedule noncritical personalization and ad work after content is interactive.

findings.summary: The LCP resource is not priority-hinted and the critical chain is long.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse says fetchpriority=high is absent on the discoverable eager LCP image; the longest network dependency chain is 2,719 ms. HAR also identified a parser-inserted high-priority script candidate.
findings.suggestedFix: Add fetchpriority=high to the LCP image and defer confirmed noncritical scripts and dependency chains.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 226,505 bytes of unused JavaScript with up to 1,630 ms savings; HAR recorded 605,982 transferred script bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by feature, load ad/video SDKs on demand, and remove duplicated or unused bundles.

findings.summary: Some semantics and alternatives are malformed or missing.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a UL with a direct SPAN child and an inappropriate role=button on a LABEL; the image audit found 5 images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use valid list children, real buttons for actions, and empty or meaningful alt attributes according to image purpose.

findings.summary: The accessibility tree is not well formed.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agent accessibility reported the menu LABEL role=button as an inappropriate role, and the list audit found invalid child structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace role-patched labels with semantic buttons and correct list markup, then keyboard-walk the resulting focus order.

findings.summary: The production viewport disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse inspected a viewport declaration containing maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no, which prevents low-vision users from zooming.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions; verify reflow at 200% and 400%.

findings.summary: Image sizing and list structure are not consistently sound.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 40 of 100 images without both dimensions; Lighthouse found invalid UL child markup.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width and height or aspect-ratio for content images and make every UL child an LI.

findings.summary: Cache policy prevents back/forward cache restoration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three BFCache blockers, including cache-control:no-store on the main resource and a cookie-modifying no-store response.
findings.suggestedFix: Use no-store only for truly sensitive responses and move personalized volatile data behind cacheable page-shell boundaries.

findings.summary: The site has no sitemap at the conventional endpoint and raw article HTML lacks its H1.
findings.evidence: /sitemap.xml returned 404. Discoverability found the article title and description in raw HTML but no raw H1, with 67% rendered-word coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish and reference an XML sitemap, and server-render the article H1 alongside its metadata.

findings.summary: Cookie transport and same-site posture is too permissive.
findings.evidence: Cookie audit found STabid without Secure and all 10 observed cookies using SameSite=None; several identifiers last 390–400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark every HTTPS cookie Secure, use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential, and shorten identifier lifetimes.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party activity start before a privacy choice.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence observed 8 third-party origins and DoubleClick on initial load; HAR attributes 69 requests and 667,124 transferred bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Block optional analytics, ad, and video SDK requests until consent; reduce vendors and batch first-party measurement.

findings.summary: Defensive response headers are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no HSTS or Permissions-Policy; Referrer-Policy is the legacy no-referrer-when-downgrade value. CSP, nosniff and frame protection are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS after subdomain readiness, deploy a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and adopt strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter.

findings.summary: The installable site does not expose an offline cache.
findings.evidence: A valid manifest and active /sw.js registration exist, but Cache Storage returned no cache names after the page loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Precache a small offline shell and recent/headline fallback, and show an explicit offline recovery state.

findings.summary: Responsive image delivery is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 61 lacked srcset and 56 below-fold images lacked lazy loading; 40 lacked complete dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive source sets, lazy-load below-fold editorial images, and retain dimensions for stable layout.

findings.summary: Nonessential work competes with the initial news experience.
findings.evidence: HAR loaded ad/video SDKs and 69 third-party requests on initial load; Lighthouse found 226 KB unused JavaScript and forced reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional SDKs behind consent and interaction, and pause/deprioritize offscreen or background processing.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes roughly half of transferred bytes.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 667,124 third-party bytes out of 1,320,746 total; IMA SDK alone transferred 154,248 bytes before a video was requested.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte budget and load video/ad SDKs only when their surface approaches the viewport or the user starts playback.

findings.summary: The public news corpus is only partly agent-ready.
findings.evidence: Robots explicitly blocks GPTBot and CCBot while allowing OAI-SearchBot and Perplexity; Lighthouse agentic browsing score is 0.5 and reports a malformed accessibility tree. No structured WebMCP capability was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep crawler policy intentional, repair the accessibility tree, and consider structured agent actions for search, topics, and article retrieval.

taskList.title: Replace forced pay-or-track gating with free, direct optional-consent rejection
Fix 360 px overflow and restore user zoom
Defer trackers, ad/video SDKs, and other optional third-party work
Harden cookies and browser security policies
Repair semantic controls, lists, image alternatives, and target sizing
Complete responsive image delivery and dimensions
Publish sitemap and server-render article H1
Apply preference-driven theming to the consent surface
Modernize component/navigation behavior and reduce feed noise
Repair agent accessibility and document intentional agent access
